fichas.title: Terminal concepts
fichas.summary: Airport terminals are selected according to gate arrangement, connections between gates and buildings, capacity, required area, and potential for extension. Modular linear terminals with satellite units are common; transporter concepts provide a lower-capacity alternative, while pier concepts require sufficient space between piers for aircraft taxiing.

Connecting terminal buildings to gates and satellite units
Transporting passengers between terminal and aircraft

fichas.title: Passenger steps and loading bridges
fichas.summary: Illustrations show mobile and integrated passenger stairs and a rotatable, extendible loading bridge. The bridge is height-adjustable to the boarding level; direct access from the terminal to aircraft is normally provided by jet bridges.
uses: Providing adjustable access between terminal and aircraft

fichas.title: Apron
fichas.summary: The apron accommodates aircraft parking and movement areas, operational roads, and parking for handling vehicles. Operational roads should connect apron and other airport operating areas efficiently and safely, with as few crossings as possible with taxiing aircraft or other operations. Roads may run in front of or behind aircraft or beside the ends of the tarmac; roads passing beneath loading bridges require clearance for handling vehicles. Mechanised and containerised aircraft handling requires sufficient space for vehicles and machinery.
uses: Connecting the apron with other airport operating areas
